description: Curated collection of free, open-access mathematics textbooks. List compiled from the AIM Open Textbook Initiative, Open Textbook Library, PreTeXt Gallery, and community recommendations.

entries.title: College Algebra 2e
entries.subject: algebra
entries.description: Comprehensive college algebra textbook covering linear equations, functions, polynomials, exponential and logarithmic functions, trigonometry, and analytic geometry. Part of the OpenStax free textbook series.

entries.title: Calculus Volume 1
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: First of three volumes covering single-variable calculus: limits, derivatives, integration, and applications. Written in the accessible OpenStax style with worked examples and exercises.

entries.title: Calculus Volume 2
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: Second of three volumes covering integration techniques, parametric equations, polar coordinates, sequences, series, and differential equations.

entries.title: Calculus Volume 3
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: Third of three volumes covering parametric equations, polar coordinates, vectors, functions of several variables, multiple integration, and second-order differential equations.

entries.title: Active Calculus — Single Variable
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: A modern, active-learning approach to single-variable calculus. Free PDF download and interactive HTML version. Designed for an active learning classroom with engaging exercises.

entries.title: Active Calculus — Multivariable
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: Continuation of Active Calculus to multivariable functions. Covers vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus.

entries.title: CLP-1 Differential Calculus
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: First of three CLP calculus textbooks from UBC. Covers limits, derivatives, and applications. Free PDF and HTML versions available.

entries.title: CLP-2 Integral Calculus
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: Second CLP calculus textbook. Covers integration techniques, applications, sequences, and series.

entries.title: CLP-3 Multivariable Calculus
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: Third CLP calculus textbook. Covers vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus.

entries.title: Calculus
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: Gilbert Strang's classic calculus textbook, available freely via MIT OpenCourseWare. Covers single variable and multivariable calculus with rich applications.

entries.title: Linear Algebra Done Right
entries.subject: linear-algebra
entries.description: The definitive open linear algebra textbook. Takes a modern, proof-based approach emphasizing linear maps over determinants. Widely adopted at top universities. Free PDF from the author's website.

entries.title: Introduction to Linear Algebra
entries.subject: linear-algebra
entries.description: Gilbert Strang's renowned linear algebra textbook, companion to his MIT OCW lecture series. Applications-focused approach with clear geometric intuition.

entries.title: A First Course in Linear Algebra
entries.subject: linear-algebra
entries.description: A well-organized linear algebra textbook with carefully constructed examples, full exercise sets with solutions, and ~90 Sage examples integrated throughout. Available in PDF and HTML.

entries.title: Linear Algebra
entries.subject: linear-algebra
entries.description: A free, open-source linear algebra textbook covering Gauss's Method, vector spaces, linear maps, determinants, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. Extensive exercise sets with worked answers.

entries.title: Notes on Diffy Qs: Differential Equations for Engineers
entries.subject: differential-equations
entries.description: A free, open-source textbook for a one- or two-semester first course in ordinary differential equations. Used at many universities with video lecture versions available.

entries.title: Elementary Differential Equations
entries.subject: differential-equations
entries.description: A classic first course in ordinary differential equations, previously published by Brooks/Cole. Free PDF and LaTeX source available. Also available with boundary value problems.

entries.title: Discrete Mathematics: An Open Introduction
entries.subject: discrete-math
entries.description: A free, open-source textbook for a first or second year undergraduate discrete math course. Features an interactive ebook version. Covers logic, set theory, combinatorics, graph theory, and more.

entries.title: Book of Proof
entries.subject: other
entries.description: An introduction to the standard methods of proving mathematical theorems. Extremely popular for transition-to-proof courses. Covers logic, sets, induction, relations, functions, cardinality, and more.

entries.title: OpenIntro Statistics
entries.subject: statistics
entries.description: A traditional introduction to statistics at the college level. Covers data collection, exploratory data analysis, probability, inference, and regression. Free PDF download.

entries.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning (ISLR)
entries.subject: statistics
entries.description: The definitive introduction to statistical learning and machine learning, with applications in R. Covers linear regression, classification, resampling, tree-based methods, SVM, deep learning, and more. Free PDF from authors.

entries.title: Introduction to Probability
entries.subject: probability
entries.description: A well-established probability textbook covering combinatorial probability, conditional probability, random variables, distributions, limit theorems, and Markov chains.

entries.title: Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications
entries.subject: other
entries.description: The gold standard open abstract algebra textbook. Covers groups, rings, fields, and Galois theory. Includes Sage integration throughout. Used at many universities nationwide.

entries.title: Basic Analysis: Introduction to Real Analysis
entries.subject: other
entries.description: A free undergraduate real analysis textbook covering the real numbers, sequences, continuity, differentiation, integration, sequences of functions, and metric spaces. Well-organized and readable.

entries.title: Measure, Integration & Real Analysis
entries.subject: other
entries.description: A graduate-level real analysis textbook published via Springer's Open Access program. Covers measure theory, Lebesgue integration, Banach and Hilbert spaces, and more. Reader-friendly style.

entries.title: A First Course in Complex Analysis
entries.subject: other
entries.publisher: San Francisco State University / Binghamton University
entries.description: A one-semester undergraduate complex analysis textbook. Covers complex numbers, analytic functions, integration, series, residues, and conformal maps.

entries.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
entries.subject: other
entries.description: Comprehensive introduction to the mathematical foundations of machine learning. Covers linear algebra, analytic geometry, matrix decompositions, vector calculus, probability, and optimization.

entries.title: Understanding Linear Algebra
entries.subject: linear-algebra
entries.description: A first course in linear algebra emphasizing geometric intuition and conceptual understanding. Built with PreTeXt, with an interactive HTML version and a clean, example-driven exposition. Covers vectors, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues, and orthogonality.

entries.title: An Infinite Descent into Pure Mathematics
entries.subject: other
entries.description: A free and open-source introductory pure mathematics textbook with a focus on logical reasoning, proof-writing, and problem-solving. Covers logic, set theory, number theory, abstract algebra, and more.

entries.title: An Infinitely Large Napkin
entries.subject: olympiad-general
entries.description: A 900-page journey through competition and advanced mathematics: olympiad algebra, combinatorics, complex analysis, topology, algebraic geometry, and beyond. Written for high school students preparing for the Putnam or IMO, and curious undergraduates. One of the most comprehensive free resources in olympiad mathematics.

entries.title: OTIS Excerpts
entries.subject: olympiad-general
entries.description: 202 curated olympiad problems with full solutions, drawn from Evan Chen's OTIS (Olympiad Training for Individual Study) coaching program. Covers all four olympiad areas (combinatorics, algebra, number theory, geometry) at USAMO/IMO level.

entries.title: Barycentric Coordinates in Olympiad Geometry
entries.subject: olympiad-geometry
entries.description: A comprehensive tutorial on using barycentric coordinates to solve olympiad geometry problems. Covers standard techniques including Conway's notation, normalized coordinates, distance formulas, and applications to concurrency, collinearity, and cyclic quadrilaterals.

entries.title: Bashing Geometry with Complex Numbers
entries.subject: olympiad-geometry
entries.description: A practical guide to solving geometry problems using complex numbers. Covers the unit circle approach, spiral similarities, the complex cross-ratio, and systematic methods for proving concurrency, collinearity, and cyclic quadrilaterals.

entries.title: Olympiad Inequalities
entries.subject: olympiad-algebra
entries.description: An introduction to the most common inequality techniques used in olympiad mathematics. Covers AM-GM, Cauchy-Schwarz, Jensen, rearrangement, Chebyshev, Schur, Muirhead, the SOS method, the UVW method, and tangent line techniques.

entries.title: Introduction to Functional Equations
entries.subject: olympiad-algebra
entries.description: A systematic introduction to solving functional equations for olympiad competitions. Covers Cauchy's equation, injectivity/surjectivity tricks, fixed point methods, monomials, and classifying solutions by common forms.

entries.title: Orders Modulo a Prime
entries.subject: olympiad-number-theory
entries.description: A focused handout on the theory of orders modulo a prime, a fundamental tool in olympiad number theory. Covers primitive roots, lifting the exponent lemma, Wilson's theorem, and applications to number theory problems.

entries.title: Expected Uses of Probability
entries.subject: olympiad-combinatorics
entries.description: A tutorial on using probabilistic methods in olympiad combinatorics. Covers linearity of expectation, the probabilistic method for existence proofs, Lovász local lemma, and applications to graph theory and extremal combinatorics.

entries.title: Monsters
entries.subject: olympiad-algebra
entries.description: A collection of pathological functional equations and their solutions. Useful for understanding edge cases, exotic functions, and the full range of behavior possible in functional equations. A companion to the main functional equations handout.

entries.title: Unofficial Syllabus for Math Olympiads
entries.subject: olympiad-general
entries.description: A comprehensive syllabus and study guide for olympiad mathematics. Covers all major topics across algebra, combinatorics, geometry, and number theory, organized by difficulty from AMC through IMO level. Essential for building a structured training plan.

entries.title: A Computational Introduction to Number Theory and Algebra
entries.subject: number-theory
entries.description: A rigorous university-level introduction to computational number theory and abstract algebra, with all the necessary mathematical background. Covers integer arithmetic, congruences, finite fields, polynomial arithmetic, primality testing, and computational aspects of groups and rings. Published by Cambridge University Press; the author provides a free PDF under a Creative Commons license.

entries.title: Algebra: Abstract and Concrete
entries.subject: abstract-algebra
entries.description: A thorough introduction to modern (abstract) algebra at a level suitable for upper-level undergraduates and beginning graduate students. Covers the conventional topics — groups, rings, fields, and linear algebra — with symmetry as a unifying theme. Offered free of charge by the author for anyone interested in learning abstract algebra.

entries.title: Real Analysis
entries.subject: real-analysis
entries.description: A graduate-level real analysis textbook covering measure theory, Lebesgue integration, differentiation, normed spaces, function spaces, and more. Formerly published by Prentice Hall (1997), this second edition includes many corrections and additions. Suitable for a two-semester graduate course.

entries.title: Elementary Real Analysis
entries.subject: real-analysis
entries.description: An undergraduate real analysis textbook formerly published by Prentice Hall (2001). Covers the real numbers, sequences, continuity, differentiation, integration, infinite series, sequences of functions, and metric spaces. Designed as a user-friendly text suitable for a one-year course.

entries.title: Mathematical Discovery
entries.subject: other
entries.description: A book about mathematics appreciation via discovery. Explores problems that resist ordinary arithmetic, algebraic, or geometric techniques and guides the reader through creative discovery methods. Covers history, unsolved problems, and includes numerous examples, illustrations, problems, and projects. Suitable for students with minimal background.

entries.title: The Calculus Integral
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: An elementary introduction to integration theory on the real line, at the level of an honor's calculus or first undergraduate real analysis course. Covers the Riemann integral and prepares the student for a graduate course in Lebesgue integration.

entries.title: Theory of the Integral
entries.subject: real-analysis
entries.description: A rigorous treatise on integration theory covering the Riemann integral, the Lebesgue integral, and the Henstock-Kurzweil integral. Serves as a sequel to The Calculus Integral. Suitable for an advanced undergraduate or graduate course.

entries.title: Probability Adventures
entries.subject: probability
entries.description: A one-semester probability text for students who have completed a one-semester college linear algebra course. Written in the style of a tabletop role-playing game, it builds probability on logic rather than set theory, with the set-theoretic approach introduced once the reader is ready. Free to download and use. Version 2023-07-21.

entries.title: Probability: Lectures and Labs
entries.subject: probability
entries.description: A one-semester probability text for students who have completed a one-semester college linear algebra course. Designed for a partially flipped classroom: roughly two-thirds lectures and one-third laboratory experiments in R. Moves rapidly through prerequisites such as set notation. Free to download and use. Version 2023-07-06.

entries.title: Online Statistics: An Interactive Multimedia Course of Study
entries.subject: statistics
entries.description: An introductory statistics resource developed at Rice University, the University of Houston-Clear Lake, and Tufts University. Presented in textbook format alongside video presentations, interactive demonstrations and simulations, case studies, and an analysis lab. The work is in the public domain, with downloadable PDF and ePub editions plus an interactive web version.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Art & Sculpture
entries.subject: geometry
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) guide exploring mathematics through art and sculpture: origami folding, sliceforms, the geometry of surfaces, symmetry, and the visual structure of two- and three-dimensional forms. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Ideas of Calculus
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) introduction to the big ideas of calculus — limits, rates of change, accumulation, and the fundamental theorem — developed through guided exploration rather than lecture. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Dance
entries.subject: other
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) guide investigating connections between mathematics and dance: symmetry and transformational geometry of movement, rhythm and pattern, and choreographic structures as mathematical objects. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Games & Puzzles
entries.subject: discrete-math
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) guide using games and puzzles to develop combinatorial reasoning, strategy analysis, induction, and mathematical thinking. Covers two-player games, Nim-style puzzles, and the mathematics of play. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Geometry
entries.subject: geometry
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) guide to geometry, starting in the imaginary world of Flatland and moving through how we see what we see, the analysis and construction of three-dimensional forms, and the geometry of space. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Knot Theory
entries.subject: other
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) introduction to the mathematical theory of knots using Tangles, exploring knot invariants, connections to well-known puzzles, and an unsolved million-dollar problem. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Music
entries.subject: other
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) guide exploring the mathematics of music: rhythm and palindromes, tuning and intervals, scales, and the wave/number theory behind musical sound. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Number Theory
entries.subject: number-theory
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) guide to number theory, investigating the intricate patterns and relationships among the integers — divisibility, primes, modular arithmetic, and classical number-theoretic ideas — through guided exploration. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Patterns
entries.subject: other
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) guide exploring how mathematics uses pattern to give structure to ideas: the naming of very large numbers (millinillitrillions), the mathematics of Islamic art, spirographs, and recurring numerical and visual patterns. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: The Infinite
entries.subject: other
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) guide to the mathematics of the infinite: very large numbers and their meaning, classical paradoxes (Zeno, the wheel of Aristotle), convergence and divergence, and the rigour surrounding infinite processes. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Discovering the Art of Mathematics: Truth, Reasoning, Certainty, & Proof
entries.subject: discrete-math
entries.description: An inquiry-based learning (IBL) guide to the distinguishing feature of mathematics — rigorous proof. Explores paradoxes, optical illusions, logical reasoning, axioms and foundations, and what it means to establish certainty and proof in mathematics. Part of the Discovering the Art of Mathematics (DAoM) liberal-arts series from Westfield State University.

entries.title: Probability and Statistics - The Science of Uncertainty
entries.subject: statistics
entries.description: A comprehensive upper-level introduction to mathematical statistics from the University of Toronto. Develops probability models, random variables, expectation, and sampling distributions, then builds the core of statistical inference: likelihood, Bayesian, and optimal inference, model checking, regression, and stochastic processes. Available as a single PDF or by chapter; a solutions manual is also provided. May be copied and distributed without alteration, with attribution, free of charge.

entries.title: Calculus in Context
entries.subject: calculus
entries.description: The Five College Calculus Course, a collaborative reform-calculus textbook emphasizing applications and context over rote manipulation. Covers single-variable calculus (including differential equations early) and extends through multivariable functions, dynamical systems, and series. The complete text is freely downloadable as one PDF or in Calculus I / Calculus II splits, with individual chapters also available.
